newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUBA LIKELY TO LIFT RATES SLIGHTLY IN 98 - INSTITUTE.
newsitem.headline: BUBA LIKELY TO LIFT RATES SLIGHTLY IN 98 - INSTITUTE.

text.p: The Bundesbank will keep interest rates unchanged in 1997 but will increase rates slightly in 1998 as economic growth and inflation pick up, a leading German economic institute predicted.

The economic slowdown during the winter of 1996/97 is likely to be only temporary as activity is likely to be boosted by increases in German exports and continued low interest rates, the Kiel Institute of World Economics said in a report.
The institute also reiterated its forecast that German gross domestic product (GDP) will grow 2.5 percent in 1997 and predicted three percent growth in 1998.

Exports are being fueled by world economic growth and by the mark's depreciation, which is likely to continue a little further, the institute said in a summary of the report released ahead of publication on Monday.

"The prospect for German exports will further improve in 1997 and will remain favourable in 1998. The economic recovery in industrial economies is likely to strengthen and the real effective exchange rate is expected to decline further, although only slightly," the institute said.

In 1998, inflation will rise slightly and the output gap -- the difference between economic output and production capacity -- will turn positive, with capacity utilisation increasing, the institute said
"In such an environment past behaviour of the Bundesbank suggests a marked increase in interest rates," it said.

"However, we expect the Bundesbank to raise interest rates only slightly, as in the run-up to EMU monetary policy in western Europe will maintain an easing bias. All in all, monetary policy will have a stimulating impact on domestic demand in 1997 as well as in 1998."

The institute said that whereas this year the economy would mainly be stimulated by exports, domestic demand would be the driving force behind the upswing in 1998 as tax rates fall due to the implementation of planned tax reforms.
